title: Internal reserve versus external ecosystem-engineering buffering
ecological_question: Do long-lived Thalassia meadows persist because of stored below-ground reserve, canopy-mediated modification of physical exposure, or both?

not_novel: rhizome carbohydrate can function as a storage reserve
seagrass canopies can modify currents, shear, sediment and light
models can couple vegetation growth/storage with hydrodynamic feedback
novelty_boundary.tampa_advance: Measure both mechanisms at the same long-monitored fixed nodes before an unopened future quantitative outcome, then estimate their independent prospective contributions to the same meadow trajectory.

sampling.frame: same synchronized 47-node Old/Middle/Lower Tampa screening used by the direct hydrodynamic design
sampling.preferred_rule: Collect TNC and paired canopy/ambient velocity at the same selected nodes and in the same predeclared baseline season/window.
primary_new_predictors: standardized node-median rhizome total non-structural carbohydrate (TNC)
sampling.requirement: Only nodes with both primary new-measurement predictors and frozen baseline controls enter the joint mechanistic-discrimination analysis.

outcome.primary: next fixed-transect survey focal_frequency minus synchronized baseline focal_frequency

joint_primary_model.formula: future_delta_frequency ~ baseline_frequency + baseline_BraunBlanquet + ambient_p90 + TNC_z + attenuation_p90_z + water_body
joint_primary_model.familywise_error: Holm correction across the two predeclared directional focal tests at family alpha 0.05.
joint_primary_model.uncertainty: node-level resampling/permutation rule frozen before future outcome access

interpretation_matrix.both_supported: Consistent with dual buffering: internal stored reserve and external canopy-mediated physical buffering each carry independent prospective information.
interpretation_matrix.tnc_only: Consistent with internal-reserve buffering beyond measured physical attenuation; hydrodynamic buffering is not independently supported.
interpretation_matrix.attenuation_only: Consistent with external biophysical buffering beyond measured reserve, but only if the separate hydrodynamic physical-function Gate A passes.
interpretation_matrix.neither: Neither measured buffer explains future quantitative state beyond baseline and ambient forcing under the frozen design.

hydrodynamic_dependency: The attenuation mechanism may be called ecosystem-engineering/self-buffering only if the direct-hydrodynamic Gate A demonstrates positive physical attenuation before future biological response access.

collinearity_boundary.report: Pearson correlation and VIF for TNC_z and attenuation_p90_z before opening the future outcome.
collinearity_boundary.consequence: Do not drop or substitute predictors after seeing the outcome. If warning threshold is crossed, retain the joint model but describe independent coefficient separation as weakly identified; standalone frozen tests remain authoritative.

interaction_rule: No TNC x attenuation interaction is a primary or rescue analysis in v1. A complementarity/redundancy interaction would require a separately powered future design.

design_sensitivity.approximation: Two-sided alpha=0.05, 80% power for one focal coefficient with six other control/predictor degrees of freedom; does not include the extra conservatism of Holm and is therefore optimistic for the joint test.
design_sensitivity.implication: 36 complete nodes is a minimum practical target for joint discrimination, not a high-power design for subtle independent effects.

claim_boundary: A supported TNC coefficient is consistent with reserve buffering but does not prove causal resource translocation.
A supported attenuation coefficient requires physical Gate A before being interpreted as canopy self-facilitation.
Do not infer dual buffering from two separate marginal associations if the joint frozen coefficients do not both pass.
Do not add an interaction, change buffer metrics, or select a favorable subset after future outcome access.
Binary re-recording is not ecological recovery.
